answer.answer:
Regulation is recorded as one of the factors driving adoption in a large share of the deployed Japanese processes here, across steel welding and erection, timber joinery cutting, concrete and shotcrete printing, inspection and material handling, but the material available describes regulation only as a named pressure on those deployments and does not itemise which statutes, codes or approvals were at issue. The one legal instrument actually named is the robot safety standard family: human-robot collaborative work is tied to compliance with robot safety requirements, and power-and-force-limiting operation within biomechanical limits is the recognised way of holding contact-injury risk down. So the practical advice is to treat safety-standard conformity as the concrete, documentable part of the regulatory problem, and to expect the rest, permitting, code compliance for the finished structure, site rules, to appear in project records only as an adoption driver you will have to investigate case by case. Note also that several of these regulation-flagged processes are already at full operational readiness, so regulation here reads as a condition of operation rather than a blocker.

**What the deployed record actually shows**

Regulation appears as an adoption factor across a wide spread of trades and materials. In steel, census_RXH5-1 performs assembly, steelwork and welding on the structural core at technology readiness level 9, adopted to address regulation [1], developed with Firm_027 as manufacturer [2]; census_RXM33-2 adds material handling to the same welding and steelwork set, at readiness level 7 [3], and is developed by Firm_066 on steel [2]. In timber, census_RXT4-1 performs assembly, material handling and timber joinery cutting on the structural core at level 9, adopted to address integration, market and regulation [4], developed by Firm_174 [2], and census_RXT5-1 works on the structural core and the envelope, facade or curtain wall, adopted to address cost and regulation [5], developed by Firm_199 [2].
